title: Nvidia board reportedly prepares to decide whether to remove CEO Jensen Huang
summary: TechCrunch, citing The Wall Street Journal, reports Nvidia's board may meet to decide Huang's future after reports linking him to a suspected Chinese spy. The share price fell about 8% after hours.
why_not_cyber: A leadership story at the leading AI chip maker, not an AI cyber incident.

title: Anthropic launches its IPO roadshow, offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 each
summary: Anthropic has started its investor roadshow for a proposed IPO of 825 million Class A shares, priced at $70 to $78 each. It has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT.
why_not_cyber: A company listing with no cyber angle.

title: Google Cloud previews Gemini for healthcare, an agent platform linked to health records, billing and prior authorisation
summary: Gemini for healthcare connects to electronic health records, billing platforms and Medicare data to run multi-step tasks such as records summaries and prior authorisation review. It is in preview with HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health and Northwell Health.
why_not_cyber: A product launch with no security evidence.

title: New York opens registration under its RAISE Act for large frontier AI developers
summary: New York opened registration for frontier developers with more than $500m revenue, who must register by 1 January 2027. They must report critical safety incidents within 72 hours and publish safety frameworks.
why_not_cyber: A general frontier AI safety law; the coverage does not mention cyber security.

title: Nvidia board opens an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort
summary: A committee of independent directors, advised by outside counsel, will oversee the review. The board says it has no reason to believe national security or Nvidia's secrets were compromised, and Huang has committed to cooperate.
why_not_cyber: A corporate governance and counter-intelligence matter with no AI cyber attack or incident.

title: Anthropic reportedly pushes ahead with a pre-Thanksgiving IPO at a lower valuation
summary: The Decoder, citing the Financial Times, reports that Anthropic plans to list before Thanksgiving, raising 80 to 100 billion dollars at a 1.25 to 1.75 trillion dollar valuation. It reports annualised revenue of about 81 billion dollars.
why_not_cyber: Stock market listing news with no cyber angle.

title: OpenAI reportedly raises a further 11 billion dollars at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation
summary: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, reports that OpenAI raised a further 11 billion dollars at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation. The round is expected to total about 20 billion dollars, short of a reported 30 billion dollar target.
why_not_cyber: Funding news with no cyber angle.

title: METR estimates Anthropic's AI R&D is improving at about twice its earlier rate, mostly because of AI
summary: METR ran a high-access evaluation inside Anthropic from 12 August to 29 October 2026. It estimates capabilities on well-specified tasks are improving at roughly twice the pre-October 2025 rate, with about 80% of the speed-up due to AI, though with wide uncertainty.
why_not_cyber: About the pace of AI research, not cyber security.

title: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base as a 280-billion-parameter open-weight model
summary: Baidu has published the weights of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base, a 280-billion-parameter base model, on Hugging Face.
why_not_cyber: No cyber evaluation published.

title: Thinking Machines Lab launches Inkling 2 Small and plans an open-weight release
summary: Inkling 2 Small is a 594B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 17B active parameters, launched with closed weights on Tinker. The company plans to release the weights under Apache 2.0 the following week, after external safety testing.
why_not_cyber: Weights not yet released and no cyber benchmark figures published.

title: US Department of Justice launches a Super Intelligence Task Force
summary: The task force will pursue misuse of advanced AI by foreign state actors, criminal groups and fraudsters, including misuse targeting critical US infrastructure. It is led by Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward and Associate Deputy Attorney General Stephen Weiss.
why_not_cyber: The announcement does not mention cyber attacks.

title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand Codex code tools
summary: OpenAI says it will acquire Pierre Computer Company, expanding Codex's tools for building, understanding and reviewing code.
why_not_cyber: An acquisition with no stated security angle.

title: OpenAI says its internal model GPT-6 Astra did worse on safety research tasks than on capability tasks
summary: OpenAI's misalignment report says GPT-6 Astra completed about 10% of hidden rubric items when coding tasks were framed as safety research, against about 16% when framed as capability research. GPT-5.6 Sol showed no such gap, and OpenAI has not yet found the cause.
why_not_cyber: An alignment finding about internal use, with no attack or incident.

title: Meta buys Conductor, maker of an app for running several AI coding agents at once
summary: Meta has bought Conductor, whose app runs several coding agents in parallel, and the team joins Meta Superintelligence Labs. Conductor Cloud goes read-only on 13 November and closes on 20 November.
why_not_cyber: An acquisition with no security element.

title: Anthropic's revised S-1 says its future models may 'imminently' meet its threshold for AI-driven acceleration of AI research
summary: Anthropic's amended S-1 filing says internal estimates indicate its future models may imminently meet its Responsible Scaling Policy definition of dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI. It warns AI-driven development could outpace its safety, alignment and security measures.
why_not_cyber: An IPO filing about AI self-improvement risk, with no specific cyber finding.

title: New York Times and three other papers sue Brave for scraping content and supplying it to AI companies
summary: The New York Times, Daily News, Chicago Tribune and Orlando Sentinel sued Brave in federal court in Manhattan. They allege Brave scraped copyrighted content into a search index and supplied it to AI companies.
why_not_cyber: A copyright case about AI training data, with no security angle.

title: OpenAI appoints former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as a national security adviser
summary: OpenAI appointed Dan Driscoll as Senior Counselor for National Security Modernization, to advise on AI for national security modernisation, cyber resilience and work with US allies.
why_not_cyber: An appointment, with no cyber finding or action.

title: GOV.UK shows DSIT split into Cabinet Office, a new business and science department, and the digital and culture department
summary: GOV.UK lists the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology as split on 2 November 2026. Its work moves to the Cabinet Office, the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, and the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.
why_not_cyber: A machinery of government change with no new cyber policy in it.

title: OpenAI reportedly cuts its funding round target after a tepid investor response
summary: Citing the Financial Times, TechCrunch reports OpenAI cut its funding target from $30 billion to $20 billion, with UAE investors leading. The Wall Street Journal reported $11 billion secured so far, at a $1.25 trillion valuation.
why_not_cyber: Funding and valuation news with no security angle.

title: Alibaba says its Qwen models will power Apple Intelligence in China
summary: Alibaba announced that Qwen will be integrated into Apple Intelligence in China, reaching the developer beta on 4 November and users with iOS 27.3 in December.
why_not_cyber: A commercial deal with no cyber evidence.

title: Microsoft offers voluntary severance to about a quarter of its workforce while shielding AI-critical teams
summary: Microsoft offered voluntary severance to about 60,000 staff at VP level and below in the US, Canada, India and the UK. Data centre, sales, cybersecurity and quantum teams are excluded.
why_not_cyber: A workforce change at a leading AI company, not a security event.

title: CMA opens a competition investigation into Meta's terms for using business website content, including for AI
summary: The CMA is investigating whether Meta's terms letting it use content from publishers' websites to build its products, including AI features, break competition law. No decision has been made and Meta has paused the rollout.
why_not_cyber: A competition case about content use, with no security angle.

title: US Justice Department asks bankruptcy court for a privacy ombudsman over possible sale of Character.AI chat data
summary: The DOJ's US Trustee office says Character.AI's privacy policy is ambiguous and may allow selling users' chat histories, including minors' and health data, in its bankruptcy asset sale. It asked for a consumer privacy ombudsman.
why_not_cyber: Privacy and bankruptcy matter, not a security incident.

title: OpenAI says it will honour a shared robots.txt signal for AI training preferences
summary: OpenAI says it will honour a shared robots.txt signal that lets website operators state their AI training preferences to participating providers.
why_not_cyber: Training data and copyright policy, no security angle.

title: Alphabet loses just over $500bn in value after saying AI search mode is cutting search ad revenue
summary: Alphabet's market value fell by just over $500bn after its chief business officer said AI mode in search was eating into ad sales.
why_not_cyber: Market and business news with no security angle.

title: OpenAI publishes an updated Model Spec with rules for agent autonomy and oversight
summary: The 29 October Model Spec says models should act only within an agreed scope of autonomy, must not self-modify or deploy persistent agents without authorisation, and must stay open to monitoring, correction and shutdown.
why_not_cyber: A model behaviour policy with no specific cyber security content.

title: Chancellor launches an independent review of NHS productivity and AI
summary: The Budget says Mark Bailie will lead an independent review of NHS productivity and AI, reporting in early 2027 to inform the next spending review. The first £15 million AI Challenge Prize competition will focus on the NHS.
why_not_cyber: AI adoption in health with no security angle.

title: noyb files complaints against Scale AI over monitoring of AI training-data workers
summary: noyb filed complaints in France, Italy, the Netherlands and Austria saying Scale AI's Outlier platform tracks freelance workers' web activity and unlawfully requires biometric checks. Scale calls the allegations unfounded.
why_not_cyber: A privacy and employment complaint, not an AI security incident.

title: Google DeepMind announces Genie 4 world model as a research preview
summary: Genie 4 generates interactive, photorealistic environments in real time with native audio. It is open to trusted testers first and is due to come to Google AI Ultra subscribers and early-access Gemini API partners.
why_not_cyber: A world-simulation model with no cyber evaluation.

title: Anthropic expands its GSA deal to offer Claude at 40% off to all levels of US government
summary: Government customers get 40% off Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the API, now extended to state, local, tribal and territorial governments. Anthropic says about 500 US government organisations use Claude.
why_not_cyber: A procurement deal; its cyber examples are customer anecdotes.

title: UK minister says Meta has delayed terms letting it crawl UK business websites for AI to 20 November, with the CMA engaging
summary: In the Lords, Baroness Ramsey said Meta has delayed updated commercial terms that would let it crawl UK business users' websites for AI development until 20 November. The CMA is engaging directly with Meta on an expedited timeline.
why_not_cyber: A copyright and competition issue, not cyber security.

title: Anthropic files S-1 for a proposed Nasdaq listing
summary: Anthropic, PBC filed a Form S-1 with the US SEC for a proposed initial public offering of Class A stock, to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. The number of shares and price range are not yet set.
why_not_cyber: A corporate finance filing with no security event.

title: AISI finds data filtering in open-weight protein models can be undone with about $80 of fine-tuning
summary: AISI found that removing viral proteins from ESM-2 training data cut viral performance, but fine-tuning on the withheld data restored it for about $80 of compute. It concludes filtering raises the cost of recovering a capability rather than removing it.
why_not_cyber: Biosecurity research, not cyber.

title: AISI finds AI coding agents can rebuild published biological AI tools from a paper for under $20
summary: In AISI's ReproBAIT evaluation with SecureBio, coding agents rebuilt simpler biological design tools from their papers within 4 hours for under $20. AISI says withholding code does not by itself control access to such a tool's capability.
why_not_cyber: Biosecurity capability research, not cyber.

title: UK government launches the AI Biosecurity Lab with up to £300 million of backing
summary: The government is setting up the AI Biosecurity Lab, backed by £100 million of public funding and up to £200 million of commitments from OpenAI, Anthropic and others. It will use frontier AI to detect biological threats earlier and speed up vaccines and treatments.
why_not_cyber: It is about biological threats, not cyber security.

title: Texas Attorney General sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over alleged harm to minors from ChatGPT
summary: Ken Paxton filed suit in Collin County accusing OpenAI of deceiving and harming Texans. He seeks an injunction that would bar minors from ChatGPT and require court-appointed review of new models.
why_not_cyber: A consumer protection and child safety case, not a security case.

title: OpenAI models come to Google Cloud
summary: Google Cloud says OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are in private preview in its Model Garden, bought through Google Cloud Marketplace. OpenAI says Microsoft remains its primary cloud partner.
why_not_cyber: A cloud distribution deal with no cyber security content.

title: Mistral releases Voxtral 3 speech models with voice cloning
summary: Mistral released Voxtral 3, a family of speech-to-text and text-to-speech models and a voice agent SDK. Its speech model can clone a voice from about 30 minutes of audio.
why_not_cyber: A product launch with no cyber evaluation or misuse evidence.

title: Two German courts hold Google liable for what its AI Overviews say
summary: Munich Regional Court I and Aachen Regional Court have treated Google's AI-generated search answers as Google's own statements. The Aachen court issued a preliminary injunction over false texts about a doctor, with fines of up to 250,000 euros per violation.
why_not_cyber: A liability ruling on AI-generated content with no security angle.

title: Canadian news publishers sue Anthropic over training data
summary: Postmedia, Torstar, The Globe and Mail and The Canadian Press have sued Anthropic in an Ontario court, alleging copyright infringement and circumvention of technical protections in training Claude. The claims have not been tested in court.
why_not_cyber: A copyright case with no security angle.

title: US sanctions five Chinese entities over the theft of Google AI trade secrets by Linwei Ding
summary: The State Department designated Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, founded by former Google engineer Linwei Ding, and four MiraclePlus entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act for significant theft of US trade secrets. OFAC added them to its Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List on 19 October.
why_not_cyber: Insider theft of AI trade secrets, with no cyber attack or AI misuse described.

title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund
summary: Anthropic plans, subject to stockholder approval, to commit 5% of its shares to a new Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, with a further 2% at the board's discretion for each 50% rise in company value above a baseline. The fund's equity cannot be used for lobbying or political giving.
why_not_cyber: Corporate governance and finance, with no security content.

title: DeepSeek releases open weights for V4.1-Flash-1017
summary: DeepSeek published MIT-licensed weights for an update to V4.1-Flash, reporting gains on reasoning, coding and agentic benchmarks. The model card gives no cyber benchmark results and no safety section.
why_not_cyber: No cyber evaluation or safety assessment was published.

title: ChatGPT Chrome extension can now read and act on open browser tabs
summary: OpenAI's updated Chrome extension lets ChatGPT read open tabs and use Computer Use in Work mode to fill in forms, on all plans.
why_not_cyber: Browser agent product launch with no security evidence published.

title: Microsoft AI describes MAI-Base-2, a 2.8T-parameter base model
summary: Microsoft AI says MAI-Base-2 is a 2.8T-parameter mixture-of-experts base model with 80B active parameters, still in post-training. It plans to license weights to trusted partners through Foundry.
why_not_cyber: A model announcement with no cyber evidence published.

title: Anthropic reports $16.8bn quarterly revenue ahead of expected listing
summary: At an investor event, Anthropic reported revenue up 45% to $16.8bn for the quarter to September and an adjusted quarterly profit, ahead of an expected stock market listing.
why_not_cyber: Business and finance news with no cyber angle.

title: Arkansas and eight other states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT safety claims
summary: Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin sued OpenAI, alleging it promoted ChatGPT as safe while knowing its risks. Attorneys general in eight other states filed similar lawsuits the same day.
why_not_cyber: Consumer protection and child safety case with no cyber security angle.

title: Former OpenAI engineer charged over hidden recording device in executive meeting room
summary: A Saudi national who worked as an OpenAI engineer was arrested on 9 October and charged over a hidden audio recorder found in an executive conference room. The complaint says a second similar device was in his bag.
why_not_cyber: Physical insider surveillance case with no AI-enabled attack or AI system involved.

title: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full
summary: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, which it calls its most capable models to date. Muse Wonder is available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code; Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers. Meta says the models were released under its Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework and that a full report with more safety evaluations will follow.
why_not_cyber: Major model launch; no cyber evidence published yet (Meta says a fuller safety report will follow).

title: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for prioritising safety
summary: Three former OpenAI safety and alignment researchers say they were fired for raising safety concerns. OpenAI says its investigation found they mishandled sensitive information and that the decision was not about safety concerns.
why_not_cyber: Staffing dispute at a leading AI company with no cyber security angle.

title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 generally available
summary: New mid-tier Claude model.
why_not_cyber: Routine model release with no cyber evidence.

title: Summary of METR's pre-deployment evaluation of Claude Opus 5.5
summary: METR's independent pre-deployment evaluation found Claude Opus 5.5 is likely a modest improvement over Fable 5.1 on AI R&D tasks and unlikely to fully automate AI R&D. The summary does not cover cyber capabilities.
why_not_cyber: Evaluation of a model release with no cyber security findings.

title: First state-level lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman
summary: Alleges ChatGPT prioritised profit over safety.
why_not_cyber: Legal action about AI safety in general, with no cyber angle.
